# Quantitative three-fiber margin from a single critical cap

This is a scoped theorem about exactly three positive-dimensional integer
fibers. It gives an actual quantitative deficit bound without any claim
that near equality of cap volumes controls their sections or shapes.

## 1. Statement and definitions

Let d>=1, and let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies satisfying

    (A+B)/2 subset K.

Let

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B),
    M=|A|+|K|+|B|,
    Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, r_d=d/(d+1).

All volumes are ordinary d-dimensional Lebesgue volumes. They equal the
corresponding d-dimensional Hausdorff measures on the fiber embeddings;
H_d(S)=M and dim_H(S)=d.

Fix y in K. Suppose the ambient closed halfspace

    H={ (z,x): u.(x-y)+alpha z>=0 },  u nonzero,

attains the raw depth Q at (0,y), where raw depth is the infimum of
H_d(S intersect G) over all ambient closed halfspaces G containing (0,y).
Write its three captured volumes as U,q,V. Thus

    Q=U+q+V.

Assume

    q>=Gamma |K|,                                         (1)
    U^(1/d)+V^(1/d)>=2(1-eta)q^(1/d),    0<=eta<=1.        (2)

For example, (1) holds if the middle trace contains the ordinary centroid
of K. Condition (2) means that the positive part of the root deficit
q^(1/d)-(U^(1/d)+V^(1/d))/2 is at most eta q^(1/d). No upper bound on the
endpoint-root sum is required.

Put

    A_eta=2(1-eta)^d,
    rho=(A_eta Gamma)^(1/d)
        =2^(1/d)(1-eta)d/(d+1).

Then the deterministic point (0,y) belongs to S and has normalized depth

    Q/M >= (1+A_eta) Gamma /
                    [1+rho^d+(2-rho)^d].                 (3)

If

    0<=eta<=1/[2(d+1)],

then this gives the explicit strict margin

    Q/M > (8/15)Gamma > (1/2)Gamma.                       (4)

Endpoint captures may be empty, supporting, proper, or full. There is no
section-area differentiability hypothesis, no homothety conclusion, and
no requirement that (0,y) maximize depth over S.

## 2. Finite integer tilts control both whole endpoint volumes

Keep u and y fixed and replace alpha by beta. The middle cap and its
volume q are unchanged. Choose L larger than the absolute values of
u.(x-y) for every x in A union B; such a finite L exists by compactness.
At beta=-L the A fiber is fully captured and the B fiber is empty. At
beta=L the A fiber is empty and the B fiber is fully captured. These
are actual ambient closed halfspaces containing the source, and the
strict choice of L removes any endpoint ambiguity. Since H attains
the raw depth,

    Q<=q+|A|,   Q<=q+|B|.

Subtracting q and using Q=U+q+V gives

    |A|>=U+V,   |B|>=U+V.                               (5)

This is the crucial comparison. It uses neither limits nor derivatives
and remains valid for every endpoint capture status. It specifically
uses the absence of any other integer fibers.

## 3. Quantitative capture and total-mass bounds

Convexity of x^d on the nonnegative reals, including the linear d=1 case,
and (2) give

    U+V >= 2[(U^(1/d)+V^(1/d))/2]^d
         >= A_eta q.

Thus (1) and (5) imply

    Q>= (1+A_eta)q >= (1+A_eta)Gamma |K|,                  (6)
    |A|,|B| >= A_eta Gamma |K|.                          (7)

Let a=|A|^(1/d), b=|B|^(1/d), c=|K|^(1/d). Whole-body BM and midpoint
inclusion give a+b<=2c. Equation (7) gives a,b>=rho c.
Moreover 0<=rho<=1: indeed the binomial theorem gives
(1+1/d)^d>=2, so Gamma<=1/2 and rho^d=A_eta Gamma<=2Gamma<=1.

For nonnegative a,b>=rho c with a+b<=2c, increase one variable until
the sum is 2c, then maximize the convex function x^d+(2c-x)^d on
[rho c,(2-rho)c]. It attains a maximum at an endpoint. Consequently

    M<= [1+rho^d+(2-rho)^d]|K|.                         (8)

Equations (6) and (8) prove (3). This argument also covers rho=0 and
rho=1; no 0^0 expression is needed.

## 4. A uniform explicit deficit threshold

Assume eta<=1/[2(d+1)]. Bernoulli's inequality gives

    A_eta=2(1-eta)^d>=2(1-d eta)>1.                     (9)

Let c_0=1-log 2, which lies in (0,1). Since
(1+1/d)^d<e, one has Gamma>e^(-1). Therefore

    rho=(2Gamma)^(1/d)(1-eta)
      >= exp(-c_0/d)(1-eta)
      >= (1-c_0/d)(1-eta)
      >= 1-c_0/d-eta.

It follows that

    (2-rho)^d <= exp[d(1-rho)]
                 <= exp(c_0+d eta)
                 < exp(3/2)/2.                         (10)

The estimates e<87/32 and exp(3/2)<9/2 have elementary exact proofs.
The exponential series through j=3 sums to 8/3, while

    sum_{j>=4} 1/j! < (1/24)sum_{j>=0}(1/5)^j=5/96.

Thus e<87/32. Also

    (87/32)^3=658503/32768 < 81/4,

the numerator gap being 5049. Hence e^(3/2)<9/2, and (10) gives

    (2-rho)^d<9/4.                                      (11)

Using Gamma<=1/2, the ratio in (3), divided by Gamma, is strictly greater
than

    (1+A_eta)/(13/4+A_eta/2).

This rational function is strictly increasing for A_eta>=0, since its
derivative has positive numerator 11/4. By (9), it exceeds its value
at A_eta=1, namely 8/15. This proves (4) in every d>=1.

## 5. Cover corollary and exact-equality specialization

Suppose finitely many depth-attaining ambient halfspaces through (0,y),
each with nonzero continuous normal, have middle traces covering K.
Assume each satisfies (2) for the same eta. At least one of their middle
traces contains the ordinary centroid of K. Ordinary Grünbaum gives
(1) for this one cap, so the one-cap theorem applies. The middle cap
volumes need not be equal.

At eta=0 the lower bound is

    Q/M >= 3Gamma / [1+2Gamma+(2-(2Gamma)^(1/d))^d].       (12)

For d>=2 it is strictly stronger than

    3Gamma / [1+Gamma+((d+2)/(d+1))^d],

because the function 1+x^d+(2-x)^d is strictly decreasing for 0<x<1,
and (2Gamma)^(1/d)>Gamma^(1/d)=d/(d+1). At d=1, (12) equals 1/2.
The d=1 value is attained by three identical intervals with the source
at the middle interval midpoint: central symmetry gives at least half
the mass in every containing halfspace, and a continuous-coordinate
cut through the midpoint gives exactly half.
For d=2, it is exactly

    12/(61-24sqrt(2)).

There is no claim of sharpness for these scoped constants.

## 6. An additional finite-tilt equalization lemma

For any depth-attaining cap with nonzero continuous normal, let its
captures be U,q,V as above, without assuming (1) or (2). As the integer
tilt beta increases, the A captured volume decreases continuously from
|A| to zero, and the B captured volume increases continuously from zero
to |B|. Continuity follows by dominated convergence because boundary
hyperplanes have zero d-volume in each full-dimensional fiber.
Thus at some finite beta_* their captured volumes agree, say both are w.

If w=0 then w<=q. If w>0, their captured bodies are full-dimensional
convex bodies. Their Minkowski midpoint is contained in the fixed middle
cap; BM gives w<=q. Comparing this cap's mass with the original minimum
therefore proves

    U+V <=2w<=2q,     Q<=3q.                            (13)

Suppose the original cap satisfies exact captured-root equality

    U^(1/d)+V^(1/d)=2q^(1/d).

Convexity gives U+V>=2q, so (13) gives equality throughout. For d>1,
strict convexity then forces U=V=q, even when proper endpoint cuts were
not assumed. For d=1 one still obtains U+V=2q and Q=3q, though individual
endpoint volumes need not agree. This establishes the equal-capture
conclusion in higher dimensions without section derivatives or BM
homothety classification.

## 7. Measure and scope audit

All halfspaces are closed ambient halfspaces. Their continuous normals
are nonzero, so their boundary in each d-dimensional fiber has zero
d-volume. The finite-tilt comparison itself uses strict saturation and
does not discard boundary mass. Intrinsic measure is exactly H_d because
all three fibers are positive d-dimensional bodies. All points used as
centroids are numerical certificates for (1); the selected source stays
(0,y) throughout. No affine lattice normalization or approximation occurs.

The theorem does not cover additional integer fibers, lower intrinsic
dimension, or a general source whose critical caps have no controlled
root deficit. Those require separate arguments for general OC.
